steps: Uncrate & fit legs

Remove the crate top, supports and plastic cover; on leg units, loosen the nuts holding the supports. Leg model: lay the stove on its back on something soft (protect the Control Board), fit each leg between the Leg Adapter flange and washer, then nut and tighten.
Optional ash cleanout
Remove the pedestal or leg ash box front cover and the top-left knock-out, fit the ash dump up through the firebox bottom over the two bolts (handle forward, on the left), and install the ash pan.

Pedestal model: remove the ash drawer front cover plate (centre screw, then lift to free the bottom tabs). Leg model: remove the two screws on either side of the leg ash box front cover. Then remove the knock-out in the top left corner of the opening.

  1. Remove the ash cleanout hole cover plate and gasket under the stove; discard the plate.
  2. Fit the provided gasket(s) around the upper tube of the ash dump mechanism.
  3. Insert it from underneath the firebox bottom, up into the hole and over the two bolts hanging down, release handle facing forward and on the left.
  4. Refit the nuts on the carriage bolts and tighten to gently compress the gasket.
  5. Install the new ash pan in the pedestal or leg ash box.

With the ash dump installed the floor firebricks go in a different layout (p. 30), leaving a gap behind the ash dump and one spare brick.
A/C adapter & battery box

Connect the adapter's barrel plug to the Control Board, then plug the adapter into a wall outlet. The optional battery box plugs into the right side of the Control Board and hooks inside the right side panel on a #8 x 1/2" screw.
Thermocouple guard
Take the thermocouple guard out of the flue collar, remove the cardboard holding the flue gas agitator in place, then refit the guard with all three ends seated.
Floor protection & clearances
Lay continuous non-combustible ember protection (USA 16" front and 8" to the sides of the door opening; Canada 18" firing side, 8" other sides) and set the stove to the clearance chart.
Chimney & connector

Use a UL-103 HT (USA) or ULC-S629 (Canada) listed chimney, or a lined masonry chimney, with a 6" flue not shared with another appliance. Minimum system height 15 feet; exit 3 feet above the roof and 2 feet above anything within 10 feet.
Install chimney & connector
Plumb-bob the flue centre to mark the ceiling and roof, clear joists and rafters, install the listed chimney to the rain cap, then fit the connector crimped end into the collar with three screws.

1. Position the floor protection and stove to the clearances.
  2. Mark the ceiling and roof hole with a string and plumb-bob hung over the exact centre of the flue.
  3. Check the location clears floor joists, ceiling joists and rafters; adjust and reconfirm clearances.
  4. Install the listed chimney from the ceiling to the rain cap per its maker's directions.
  5. Slip the crimped edge of the connector inside the stove collar and secure with three screws through the collar holes.
  6. Stack the remaining pipe to the chimney and join with the manufacturer's approved adapter; a slip section helps.

Up-and-out installs: minimum first section of pipe 12" [300mm]. The unit may be harder to start, so give the first section as much vertical length as possible. Offsets: at least three sheet metal screws per joint, supported by the chimney maker's listed offset support. The venting figures show a minimum 7' [2.1m] ceiling height.

Through a combustible wall (NFPA 211-2024, p. 25 to 26): System A, 12 in. (305mm) to combustibles; System B, 9 in. (229mm); System C, 6 in. (152mm); System D, 2 in. (51mm). Maintain the vapour barrier wherever the chimney penetrates to the exterior.
Combustion air

Outside air is necessary in mobile homes and optional in houses: a 4" (100mm) inlet through the floor or the wall behind, with rodent screen. A house install using outside air must secure the stove to the structure.
Mobile home
Not in a sleeping room. Anchor with two 1/4-20 x 2" or longer lag screws, use outside air, a listed double-wall connector and listed chimney, and no horizontal connector.

• A competent or certified installer is strongly recommended.
  • Do not install in a sleeping room. Do not connect to a flue serving another appliance.
  • Maintain the structural integrity of the floor, wall and ceiling/roof.
  • Anchor with two 1/4-20 x 2" or longer lag screws: leg model through the supplied leg anchors hooked around each leg's levelling bolt; pedestal model through the holes in the sides of the base.
  • Outside air supply is required (outside air kit).
  • Listed double-wall connector and a ULC-S629 or UL-103HT listed chimney; horizontal connector not permitted.
  • Clearances are the double-wall values: 8" side wall, 8" back wall, 5" corner (Figure 25).
Optional blower
Kit 11140001 can be installed any time: remove the five screws on the rear heat shield cover plate, follow the kit's instructions and route the cord away from the heater, never beneath it.

light.title: Lighting a fire
light.html:
Never use chemicals or any other volatile liquid to start a fire.

  1. Set the air control to High (all the way to the left) and open the door.
  2. Put crumpled newspaper in the centre of the firebox. Crisscross several pieces of small, dry kindling over it and add a few pieces of larger kindling on top.
  3. Light the paper. Leave the door open about 1/2" (13mm) to 1" (25mm) until the kindling is fully in flames. Never leave the stove unattended with the door open.
  4. Once the kindling is fully in flames, add a few small pieces of wood and close the door.
  5. When there's a good bed of coals and the wood has charred, switch to normal burning (see Air control and reloading).

Build the fire right on the firebricks. Don't raise it on a grate or andirons.

Your first two or three fires: the paint is baking on, so expect some smoke and smell. Open windows and doors and keep the room well ventilated. Smoke detectors may go off more often for now. Don't disconnect them. Follow the Stove Bright paint sheet that came with the stove.

air.title: Air control, reloading and overnight burns
air.html:
The air control sits under the ash lip at the front. Facing the stove, it runs from Low (right) to High (left), with Medium in the middle. Set it anywhere in between for the heat you want.

Loading

Use logs up to 18" (457mm) long, laid parallel to the stove front so air can flow between them. Always use dry wood, and don't load so high that wood could fall out when you open the door.

Reloading

  1. Set the air to High and give the fire time to brighten.
  2. Open the door slowly so smoke doesn't puff out.
  3. Add wood and burn on High for about 10 to 15 minutes, until it's fully charred.
  4. Then set the air where you want it.

Overnight

Use unsplit logs. Char the load completely on High, then slowly turn the air to Low. Never try an overnight burn with green or wet wood. To restart, rake the hot embers to the front, add a couple of dry split logs, close the door and set the air to High. Once they've charred, reset the air.

Don't run it on High for long, and don't over-fire the stove. High is for lighting and charring fresh wood; too long on High risks over-firing. A glowing red top or vent pipe means you're over-firing, which can permanently damage the stove and chimney.

wood.title: What wood to burn
wood.html:
Burn natural wood only. Air-dried, seasoned hardwood generally burns more efficiently and cleaner than softwood or green wood. Season wood for six months or more and store it under cover, away from open flame or heat.

Ideal length16 inches
Maximum length18 inches

Never burn

  • Wet, green or unseasoned wood, salt water wood, treated wood or railroad ties
  • Garbage, lawn clippings or yard waste, manure or animal remains
  • Coal or charcoal, solvents, waste petroleum products, paints, paint thinners or asphalt products
  • Anything with rubber (tires included), plastic or asbestos, or construction or demolition debris
  • Paper products, cardboard, plywood or particleboard

Burning any of these may release toxic fumes, or make the stove ineffective and cause smoke. Other fuels, such as charcoal, can produce large amounts of carbon monoxide, a tasteless, odourless gas that can kill.

Fire starters made from paper, cardboard, sawdust or wax are fine for lighting.

Note: on wet wood, the manual's p. 6 lists wet, green and unseasoned wood among the things not to burn, and says wood that sizzles, hisses and blackens without lighting in five minutes is too wet to burn. Its p. 8 says that if you feel it is necessary to burn wet or unseasoned wood, do so only with the air inlet set open enough to maintain a good strong fire and fairly high chimney temperatures, and never overnight with green or wet wood.

Is it dry? A quick test

Put a large piece on a good bed of coals. Burning on more than one side within one minute: dry. Turns black and lights within three minutes: damp. Sizzles, hisses and blackens without lighting in five minutes: too wet to burn. A moisture meter can confirm.

Wet wood can cut heat output by up to 25% and builds creosote fast. Salt water wood and garbage also eat away metal and void the warranty.

ash.title: Removing and disposing of ashes
ash.html:
Only remove ashes when the stove is cold. When the ash is 3" (76mm) to 4" (102mm) deep and the fire has burned down and cooled, take out the excess. Leave about 1" (25 mm) on the firebox floor to help keep a hot bed of coals.

With the ash dump (optional on the Vista LE2)

  1. The handle is under the ash lip on the left. Pull it out 1/2" (13mm) and turn it clockwise to unlock the ash dump.
  2. Hold the handle open and pull ashes into the opening. Leave large embers; they still hold heat.
  3. Release the handle and push it in to lock. Make sure the ash dump door is fully closed, then fill the opening with leftover ash, level with the floor.
  4. Lift and pull out the ash pan, empty it into a metal container, and seat the pan back properly.
Never burn with the ash dump door open. It creates a hazardous condition.

Disposing of ashes

Use a metal container with a tight-fitting lid. Set it on a non-combustible floor or on the ground, well away from anything that can burn, and keep it closed until every cinder has cooled. Don't put other waste in it.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Clean the glass only when the stove is cold, with fireplace glass cleaner. Don't use abrasive cleaners, and never scrape it with anything that could scratch.

What the deposit tells you

  • Light brown, dusty, wipes off easily: good burning and dry wood, so your pipes and chimney are likely fairly clean.
  • Black, greasy, hard to remove: wet or green wood, or burning too slowly. The same build-up is forming at least as fast in your chimney.

Glass that keeps getting dirty can also mean the door gasket is leaking. Check the door latch and replace the gasket if needed.

Door and glass care

  • Don't slam the door, and make sure no logs stick out to hit the glass.
  • If the glass cracks or breaks, replace it before you use the stove. Use only 10-1/2" (266mm) x 16-1/2" (419mm) x 5 mm ceramic glass from your dealer.
  • Clean the plated door with mild soap and water only. Abrasive cleaners void the warranty.
Hot glass will cause burns. Don't touch it until it has cooled, and never let children touch it.

chimney.title: Creosote and chimney fires
chimney.html:
Slow, smoky fires leave tar in the cool chimney as creosote. Built-up creosote can catch fire and burn extremely hot.

Check and clean

  • Inspect the chimney connector and chimney at least once every two months in the heating season. Remove creosote once it reaches 3 mm or more.
  • Until you know your stove, check daily. Weekly cleaning may be needed in mild weather; monthly is usually enough in the coldest months.

Burn clean

Load small amounts (two or three logs, or 1/4 to 1/2 of a full load) and leave the air fairly wide open for the first 10 to 30 minutes after each loading. Use dry, seasoned wood.

Signs of a chimney fire

Flames or sparks shooting out of the top of the chimney, a roaring sound, or the chimney vibrating.

  1. Get everyone ready to leave, with a meeting place outside.
  2. Close the air inlet on the stove.
  3. Call the fire department. Keep a fire extinguisher handy.
  4. Afterwards, have the chimney cleaned and checked for stress and cracks before your next fire, and check nearby combustibles and the roof.

A certified chimney sweep is strongly recommended for inspection and service.

safety.title: Safety around the stove
safety.html:
• The stove is hot while it's running. Keep children, clothing and furniture away; touching it can burn skin.
  • Keep the loading door closed while it burns, and open it only to add wood. Keep the ash dump closed too.
  • Never use gasoline, lantern fuel, kerosene, charcoal lighter fluid or similar liquids to start or "freshen up" a fire. Keep them well away from the stove.
  • Build fires right on the firebricks, never on a grate or andirons. Replace broken or missing bricks.
  • Keep wood, furniture, newspapers and other things that burn out of the clearance area and the space you need for loading and ash removal.
  • Don't alter the air control or its factory-set low burn rate. Tampering voids the warranty, and changing the setting is against federal regulations.
  • Never barbecue in the stove.
Do not over-fire the stove. Trying to get more heat than the stove is designed to give can permanently damage the stove and chimney. A glowing red top or vent pipe, or a glowing chimney or connector, means you are over-firing. Don't leave an over-firing condition uncorrected: it can be hazardous and may void the manufacturer's warranty. Don't run the stove on High for long periods.
Smoke and carbon monoxide detectors are strongly recommended where the stove is installed. Make sure everyone at home knows how to run it and what to do in a chimney fire.

maintain.title: Weekly and monthly checks
maintain.html:
Look for cracks, heavy corrosion, burned-out sections and bad warping.

Weekly

  • Firebrick: look for cracking.
  • Door gasket: sagging, out of place or damaged.

Monthly

  • Brick rails and their tabs
  • Air riser tube at the back of the firebox
  • Back side of the airwash chamber
  • Baffle locking pin and baffle tubes (at the top of the firebox)

When the chimney is cleaned

  • Top baffle board and blanket, baffle, baffle tubes and baffle gasket
  • Top heat shield and its mounting bolts, and the brick rails
Baffle warpingup to 1/4" (.65cm) is normal
Door gasket7/8" (22mm) fiberglass rope, kit 80000156
Optional blowervacuum at least every six months

Replace the baffle if it's warped more than that, cracked or broken. Use only parts supplied by the manufacturer. If you find damage, call your dealer: running the stove with broken parts can damage other parts and may void your warranty.

Never run the stove with the baffle, baffle tubes, insulation or flue gas agitator removed.

power.title: Power, status lights and the blower
power.html:
The stove's control board plugs into a wall outlet through an A/C adapter.

Reset: if you unplug the stove, or the power flickers and the control board freezes, unplug the adapter from the wall, wait at least 30 seconds, then plug it back in.

Power outages

With the optional battery box, the stove stays fully working in a power failure; batteries last an estimated 5-7 days of continuous use. With no power and no batteries, it still runs within safe, certified limits on the manual air control.

To change batteries, lower the battery box (right side, below the side panel), release the catch, lift off the cover and swap the batteries. Don't pull on the wires.

Status lights

On the control board at the back, only the blue (programmed) and green (power) lights should be on. Red means the firebox temperature sensor (thermocouple) is disconnected or not working; yellow means the flue collar one is. Call your dealer.

Optional blower

Set the rocker switch on the fan housing to Auto and it comes on as the stove heats up and shuts off once it has cooled. Man runs it until you turn it off. With the air on Low, run the blower on Low.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
For the original registered purchaser:

Limited lifetime (10 years), parts onlyporcelain finish, glass (thermal breakage only, not impact), plating, firebox, baffle
3 year comprehensive, parts and laborany defective part, including blowers, speed controls and thermal switches

Not covered

  • Firebrick, gaskets and ceramic fiber blankets
  • Firebox rails and heat shields (excluded from lifetime coverage)
  • Labor under the lifetime coverage
  • Misuse, abuse, improper installation, accident, lack of maintenance or modification

Excessive draft, heating too large an area, or contaminated fuel (high sodium, plastics, chemicals) may also void it. Porcelain is warranted for gloss retention; some colours darken when hot and return to their shade when cool.

Making a claim

Report the problem to your Pacific Energy dealer with proof of purchase, the purchase date, and the model name and serial number (on the certification label and the manual cover).

Register your stove at pacificenergy.net/register. This is a summary; the full terms are in the manual.

specModels.title: Models covered
specModels.html:
One manual covers both models. Its figures are captioned "VISTA LE2", including the dimensions figure that also shows the Vista Classic LE2.

Vista LE2pedestal model or leg model; ash cleanout optional
Vista Classic LE2porcelain enamel top, sides and ash shelf; cast trivet
Emissions, both models1.6 g/hr

Classic enamel colours in the parts list: Ebony Black, Ivory, Sunset Red, Modern Desert, Midnight Blue. Trivet: Metallic Black or Nickel. Vista LE2 door castings: Black, Nickel or Brushed Nickel.

Maker's website: Porcelain enamel: choice of six colors; Enamel colours shown: Black, Evergreen, Ivory, Midnight Blue, Modern Desert, Sunset Red.

Overall dimensions are drawn separately for the Vista LE2 pedestal, Vista LE2 leg and Vista Classic LE2 on this page. The text doesn't say which figure is height, width or depth, so read them off the drawing.

The manual gives no separate output, clearance or floor-protection numbers for the Vista Classic LE2. The rating label's connector clearances are listed for VISTA LE2 (and ALDERLEA T4 LE2, a different stove on the same label).

specOutput.title: Output and efficiency
specOutput.html:
EPA BTU output (efficiency table)12,115 to 30,149 btu/hr.
Heat delivered under test (text)12,300 to 30,150 Btu/hr
Maker's website: EPA Test Fuel 30,150 BTU.
LHV tested efficiency82%
HHV tested efficiency75%
Maker's website: Efficiency (HHV) 75.4%.

Efficiencies are weighted averages tested to CSA B415. The BTU range is based on that efficiency and the burn rates from the low and high EPA tests using Douglas Fir dimensional lumber.

Note: the manual gives the output range as 12,115 to 30,149 btu/hr in the efficiency table and 12,300 to 30,150 Btu/hr in the text on the same page (p. 3).

specFuel.title: Fuel and emissions
specFuel.html:
FuelSeasoned cord wood
Ideal wood length16 inches
Maximum wood length18 inches
EPA certified emissions1.6 grams per hour
CO emissions1.4 grams per minute

Meets the U.S. EPA 2020 crib wood emission limits for wood heaters sold after May 15, 2020, using Method 28R. CO varies with fuel and how the unit is operated. Logs load parallel to the stove front; burn directly on the firebrick, no grate.

specFlue.title: Flue and chimney
specFlue.html:
Stove outlet / flue6 inches
Connector6 inch / 150MM min. 24 MSG black, or listed
USAUL-103 HT listed connector and chimney
CanadaULC S-641 listed double-wall connector, ULC-S629 listed chimney
Min. system height15 feet (4.6 m.) from base of appliance
Flue exit3 feet (1 m.) above roof; 2 feet (0.6 m.) above highest projection within 10 feet (3 m.)
Single-wall connector to combustibles18 inches / 455MM (rating label, p. 3)

A lined masonry chimney suitable for solid fuel, in good condition, is also allowed. Don't connect to a flue serving another appliance or to any air distribution duct, and don't install in a fireplace. Reducing or increasing the flue size may hurt performance.

Single-wall pipe: as short and straight as possible, clean and new, crimped ends down, three sheet metal screws at every joint and collar. Never through an attic, roof space, closet or similar concealed space, floor or ceiling; wall passes per CAN/CSA-B365 or NFPA 211. The 18-inch clearance may be reduced with listed pipe shields, wall protectors or other means approved locally.

specClear.title: Clearances to combustibles
specClear.html:
Minimum clearances from the rating label (p. 3) and Figure 18 (this page):

Side wall to unit10" single wall · 8" double wall
Back wall to unit10" single wall · 8" double wall
Corner to unit7" single wall · 5" double wall
Combustibles in front of the unit48" [1.2 m] (venting figures, p. 23)

Connector clearances (rating label, VISTA LE2)

Side wall to connector19-1/2" single · 17-1/2" double
Back wall to connector14-3/8" single · 12-3/8" double
Corner to connector16-1/2" single · 14-1/2" double

Single-wall values are "as tested"; a pipe shield may be required locally. Mobile homes use the double-wall values only (Figure 25, p. 27). For close clearances use a listed double-wall connector. Clearances may be reduced with heat shielding approved under CSA B365 or NFPA 211 and by local authorities.

Note: the rating label (p. 3) gives the connector clearances above; the Figure 18 drawing on p. 20 prints 17 3/8", 19 7/8" and 22 7/8" (single wall) and 15 3/8", 17 7/8" and 20 7/8" (double wall) around the connector without saying what each one measures.
Note: the rating label (p. 3) gives a combustible alcove of 3 ft max. depth, 6 ft min. height and 41-3/4" min. width; Figures 18 and 25 (p. 20 and p. 27) give an alcove min. height of 7' (2.13m) and max. depth of 3' (915 mm).

specFloor.title: Floor protection
specFloor.html:
The stove may sit on a combustible floor with continuous non-combustible ember protection extending:

USA · front16" (406 mm) to the front of the fuel loading door opening
USA · sides8" (203 mm) to the sides of the door opening
USA · minimum size33 3/8" (850mm) wide × 35" (890mm) overall depth
Canada · firing side18" (457 mm)
Canada · other sides8" (203 mm)
Canada · minimum size40 3/4" (1.035m) wide × 45" (1.14 m) overall depth

In the USA, protection is also required under a horizontal chimney connector and 2" (51 mm) beyond each side. Don't obstruct the space beneath the heater.

The rating label (p. 3) also lists floor-protection distances by letter (G, H, I), keyed to its own drawing and measured from points the text doesn't state. Check them against the label.

specAir.title: Combustion air
specAir.html:
Outside airnecessary for mobile homes, optional for residential
Inlet / duct4" (100mm) metal flex or air intake
Rodent screen (pedestal floor hole)4" x 4" (100 mm x 100 mm)

Through the floor

From a ventilated crawl space, or ducted outdoors. Leg model: hole for 4" metal flex behind the ash box enclosure; fit the 4" Intake Starter to the ash box enclosure and run 4"(100mm) i.d. metal flex to the floor. Pedestal model: 4" (100mm) hole anywhere inside the pedestal perimeter, rodent screen stapled or nailed over it, rear cover left on.

Through the wall behind

4"(100mm) air intake through the wall. Leg model: Intake Starter over the hole in the rear of the ash box enclosure. Pedestal model: move the rear cover plate to the hole under the pedestal, then fit the Intake Starter at the rear. Run metal flex to the inlet.

Room air: the stove draws through the opening in the ash box enclosure. Residential outside air requires the stove to be secured to the structure so the duct can't dislodge.

Keep the room well ventilated; anything causing negative pressure can pull fumes into the living area. In extreme cold with slow burns, the upper part of an exposed chimney can ice up and block flue gases.

specElec.title: Electrical
specElec.html:
Blower kitPart # 11140001, three prong power cord
Electrical rating (p. 28)115 volts AC-1.02 amps
Fan electrical rating (label, p. 3)115V, 60HZ, 1.0 AMP
Fan output140 CFM
Control board powerA/C adapter (Wall Adapter 12V, 80002838)
Optional battery box11490005, est. 5-7 days continuous use

Install the blower through the rear heat shield cover plate (five screws), per the kit instructions. Route the cord away from the heater, never beneath it. Auto switches the fan with stove temperature; Man bypasses the sensor and runs until switched off. Air on L: blower on Low; between L and H: any speed.

Note: the manual gives the blower current as 1.02 amps on p. 28 and 1.0 AMP on the rating label (p. 3).

review.notes: Model split: one manual and one set of ratings, clearances, floor protection and venting for both models; figures are captioned 'VISTA LE2' (Figure 1 'VISTA LE2 dimensions' includes the VISTA CLASSIC LE2 drawing, so the caption is used for the family). Text differences only: Vista LE2 comes as pedestal or leg model and the ash cleanout is 'optional on VISTA LE2' (p. 9); Vista Classic LE2 has its own enamel top/side/ash shelf and trivet parts (p. 33). The rating label lists connector clearances for VISTA LE2 and ALDERLEA T4 LE2 only; the Classic isn't named in that table. Dimensions (p. 13) are drawing-only (no height/width/depth labels in the text) so no per-model dimension rows were transcribed. In doc1.txt the p. 3 Efficiency and BTU Output table is scrambled; the LHV 82% / HHV 75% pairing and the table's 12,115 to 30,149 btu/hr were confirmed from the raw text extraction of the same page (unit.json raw_path). Rating-label floor-protection letters G/H/I (USA 16/5/0 in., Canada 18/8/8 in.) are keyed to the label drawing and not transcribed; the p. 19 text is used. Label and Figure 18 mm conversions differ slightly (254 vs 255 mm, 203 vs 205 mm, 178 vs 180 mm, 127 vs 130 mm); the guide shows inches. Figure 18 prints 17 7/8" as 505mm (same mm as 19 7/8"). Figure 1 and Figure 18 lettering aside, the p. 23 callouts used (48" combustibles in front, 12" minimum first section of pipe, 7' ceiling height) are labelled in text. The manual's internal cross-references are off by about a page (e.g. 'Baffle Removal page 11' is p. 12, clearances 'Page 18 or 19' are p. 19-20, 'see page 8, Proper Draft' is p. 9); links use physical pages. Parts list p. 33 gives 80002882 for both 'Side, Vista Classic LE2, Ebony Black' and 'Ash Shelf, Vista Classic LE2, Midnight Blue' (likely a typo; no enamel part numbers used). Not in the manual, so not checked against the catalog: firebox volume, weight, heating area, burn time, max cordwood BTU, glass area, battery type/count, non-catalytic wording. Website differences shown as Maker's website notes and listed in catalog_mismatches: Efficiency (HHV) 75.4% vs the manual's HHV 75%; EPA Test Fuel 30,150 BTU (matches the p. 3 text, not the table's 30,149); six enamel colours including Evergreen vs five in the parts list. The control-board light meanings (p. 32) are given as the codes table. French label text duplicates the English; nothing was translated.
